headline: Fleming found penicillin, Mickey Mouse arrived in November, and fifteen nations signed away war
texture: Alexander Fleming noticed that a mould had killed the bacteria in a dish he had left out, which turned out to be the first true antibiotic. Fifteen nations signed the Kellogg-Briand Pact in Paris on August 27, renouncing war as an instrument of policy, and the signatures held for about a decade. Stalin launched the first five-year plan on October 1. Herbert Hoover won the presidency on November 6 by a wide margin.

Mickey Mouse made his official debut in Steamboat Willie on November 18, with sound cut to the picture. The Singing Fool took $3,821,000 in rentals, twice what any silent managed, and Al Jolson was in that one too. Chaplin's The Circus came second and was silent. The argument about whether talking pictures were a novelty was effectively over by December.

Schenectady got the first regular schedule of television programming on May 10, and a melodrama called The Queen's Messenger went out by television on September 11, the first play broadcast that way. Amelia Earhart crossed the Atlantic by air on June 17 and 18, the first woman to do it. Thomas Hardy died in January and Hendrik Lorentz in February.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the three price series all start later. No awards section: the first Academy Awards ceremony was held in 1929, where the film.awards window opens, and it honoured films from this year and the one before. Penicillin carries no date because the source states the discovery without dating it. The Kellogg-Briand signatures holding for about a decade is a judgement rather than a sourced claim, and comes out if challenged.
